requirements: Reproduce the core contributions of 'Deep Kernel Fusion for Transformers' — the DeepFusionKernel operator, its profiler-driven scheduler, its integration with SGLang, and the reported throughput speedups on A100 and H100 GPU clusters for LLaMA 3.1 70B inference workloads.

verification.spec: Run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total --format=csv` and assert exactly 4 GPUs are listed, each with 'A100' in the name and memory.total >= 80000 MiB. Also verify SXM form factor via `nvidia-smi -q | grep 'Product Brand\|Board Part Number'`.

sub_tasks.requirements: PCIe Gen4 links (64 GB/s) between GPUs and host are present and verifiable, and NCCL is configured to use NVLink where available for all-reduce collectives across TP=4.

verification.spec: Query `nvidia-smi topo -m` and parse the topology matrix; assert at least one GPU-GPU link is NVLink (NV#) and any non-NVLink GPU-GPU or GPU-CPU link is PCIe. sub_tasks.requirements: The same inter-device reduction strategy (SGLang's custom cross-device all-reduce kernels) is used across all baseline and DeepFusionKernel measurements to isolate fusion effects from communication effects.

verification.spec: Inspect the SGLang launch configuration used for every measurement (baseline, DeepFusionKernel, vLLM comparison) and verify the same all-reduce implementation is selected — i.e., SGLang's custom all-reduce kernels are enabled (not disabled via --disable-custom-all-reduce) for both baseline and DFK runs. Assert the config flag is identical across runs by diffing the launch commands.

sub_tasks.requirements: The tensor-parallel partitioning scheme for the SwiGLU MLP (W_Up and W_Gate column-wise, W_Down row-wise, single all-reduce per block) is implemented consistently with the paper's Figure 2 and Section A.1.
Column-wise sharding of W_Up and W_Gate is implemented so that each of the TP=4 ranks holds a contiguous slice of the d_ff dimension.
Code has been implemented that constructs sharded W_Up and W_Gate tensors on each rank whose local d_ff dimension equals d_ff / TP (i.e., column-parallel partitioning of the (d_model, d_ff) weight).

verification.spec: Import the DeepFusionKernel MLP module and instantiate it with LLaMA 3.1 70B dimensions (d_model=8192, d_ff=28672) under TP=4. On each rank, assert local W_Up and W_Gate parameter shapes are (d_model, d_ff/TP) = (8192, 7168) or transposed equivalent. Assert d_ff % TP == 0 and that the sum of local d_ff shards across ranks equals the global d_ff.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that loads/initializes LLaMA 3.1 70B W_Up and W_Gate weights and distributes them column-wise across the 4 TP ranks with no cross-rank overlap and full coverage of the full weight matrices.

verification.spec: Load LLaMA 3.1 70B W_Up and W_Gate into the DeepFusionKernel TP=4 layout. Gather the sharded weights from all 4 ranks and concatenate along the d_ff dimension; assert the concatenated tensors are exactly equal (allclose atol=0) to the original unsharded W_Up and W_Gate. Also assert the per-rank shards are disjoint slices (no overlap in indices).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the column-parallel W_Up and W_Gate GEMMs take the full replicated input activation X (of shape (M, d_model)) as input on each rank, without an input all-gather.

verification.spec: Instrument the DeepFusionKernel MLP forward to record all NCCL/collective calls made during a forward pass on TP=4. Feed a replicated input X of shape (M=4, d_model=8192) that is identical on every rank. Assert: (a) no all_gather is called before the up/gate GEMMs, (b) the up_proj and gate_proj GEMMs receive an input tensor whose first-dim shape is (M, d_model) with no sharding on d_model, and (c) exactly one all_reduce is called after down_proj.

sub_tasks.requirements: Row-wise sharding of W_Down is implemented so that each rank consumes only its local slice of the intermediate activation.
Code has been implemented that shards W_Down row-wise so that each rank holds a (d_ff / TP, d_model) slice, matching the column-parallel output layout of the (SiLU(W_Gate X) * (W_Up X)) intermediate.

verification.spec: Instantiate the TP=4 SwiGLU MLP module for LLaMA 3.1 70B shapes (d_model=8192, d_ff=28672) and assert the W_Down weight tensor on each rank has shape (28672/4, 8192) = (7168, 8192), confirming row-wise sharding along the d_ff dimension.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the local W_Down GEMM on each rank produces a partial (M, d_model) output tensor from its local intermediate activation shard, with no intermediate all-gather on the d_ff dimension.

verification.spec: Trace/inspect the forward pass of the TP-sharded SwiGLU block: assert that on each rank the local W_Down GEMM takes an input of shape (M, d_ff/TP) and produces a partial output of shape (M, d_model) without any all-gather being called on the d_ff dimension between the fused kernel and W_Down. Use a monkey-patched collective op to detect any all-gather calls with d_ff-sized tensors.

sub_tasks.requirements: The SiLU nonlinearity and elementwise gate multiplication are executed entirely on each rank's local shard without cross-device communication.

Code has been implemented such that SiLU(W_Gate X) and its elementwise multiplication with (W_Up X) operate on the local (M, d_ff / TP) shard on each rank, with no collective operations invoked between the first GEMMs and W_Down.

verification.spec: Monkey-patch torch.distributed.all_reduce/all_gather to record calls, run the SwiGLU block forward once with TP>=2, and assert zero collective calls occurred between the Up/Gate GEMMs and W_Down. Verify intermediate SiLU*Up tensor has shape (M, d_ff/TP) on each rank.

sub_tasks.requirements: Exactly one all-reduce collective is issued per SwiGLU MLP block, aggregating the partial W_Down outputs across TP ranks.
Code has been implemented that performs a single all-reduce (sum) on the (M, d_model) partial output tensor after the W_Down GEMM, producing the final replicated SwiGLU block output on every rank.

verification.spec: Instantiate the TP=4 SwiGLU MLP module on 4 ranks with dummy weights. Monkey-patch torch.distributed.all_reduce to count invocations and record tensor shape. Run one forward pass and assert exactly 1 all_reduce call was made, with the reduced tensor shape (M, d_model) and op=SUM. Verify the output is bit-identical across all ranks.

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral test verifies that exactly one collective communication call (one all-reduce, and zero all-gathers or reduce-scatters) is invoked per SwiGLU MLP block during a decoding step under TP=4.

verification.spec: Monkey-patch torch.distributed collective ops (all_reduce, all_gather, reduce_scatter, broadcast) to counters. Run one SwiGLU MLP block forward under TP=4 and assert counter[all_reduce]==1 and counter[all_gather]==counter[reduce_scatter]==0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The implementation reuses SGLang's existing all-reduce / collective primitives for the SwiGLU block's post-W_Down aggregation rather than introducing a new communication routine.

verification.spec: Grep the DeepFusionKernel integration source for imports of collective primitives; assert they resolve to sglang.srt.distributed (or equivalent SGLang) modules, not custom NCCL wrappers. Confirm the post-W_Down all-reduce uses the same tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce function as the baseline SGLang implementation.

sub_tasks.requirements: The distributed SwiGLU MLP produces numerically correct outputs matching a single-device reference implementation.

A correctness test confirms that the TP=4 SwiGLU MLP output (after the single all-reduce) matches a single-GPU reference SwiGLU forward pass on identical inputs to within FP16 numerical tolerance across all ranks.

verification.spec: Construct a full-precision reference SwiGLU MLP on a single GPU with weights W_Up, W_Gate, W_Down. Shard the weights column-wise (Up, Gate) and row-wise (Down) across 4 ranks, run the TP=4 forward including the final all-reduce, and gather the output on rank 0. Assert torch.allclose(tp_output, ref_output, atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2) in FP16.

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral check verifies that the TP-partitioned SwiGLU MLP performs the same number of floating-point operations per rank as expected under column-parallel/row-parallel sharding (i.e., no duplicated GEMM work introduced by the partitioning scheme).

verification.spec: Compute expected FLOPs per rank as 2*M*d_model*(d_ff/TP)*2 (Up+Gate) + 2*M*(d_ff/TP)*d_model (Down) + O(M*d_ff/TP) elementwise for TP=4 with LLaMA 70B shapes. Instrument the fused kernel (or count via analytic trace) and assert measured FLOPs match this expectation within 1%, confirming no duplicated GEMM work.

sub_tasks.requirements: Row-major and column-major tiling variants of DeepFusionKernel are implemented, with tile sizes tuned to balance register usage, shared-memory occupancy, and Tensor Core utilization, exposing a set of candidate kernels.
The kernel source exposes multiple candidate variants distinguished by loop ordering (row-major vs column-major tiling) so the scheduler can select among them.

Code has been implemented that defines at least two distinct DeepFusionKernel variants (one row-major-tiled, one column-major-tiled) as separately callable kernels or as a single kernel parameterized by a loop-order template/flag.

verification.spec: Import the kernel module and enumerate the exposed kernel entrypoints/variants. Assert at least two distinct variants exist: one row-major-tiled and one column-major-tiled, either as two separate callables or as a single kernel accepting a loop-order/template flag with at least two valid settings. Each variant must be independently invocable and produce numerically equivalent output on a small test case.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that registers all tiling/loop-order variants into a candidate-kernel list or registry that the profiler-driven scheduler can enumerate at deployment time.

verification.spec: Import the candidate-kernel registry (e.g., KERNEL_CANDIDATES list/dict) from the DeepFusionKernel module and assert it contains >=2 entries covering row-major and column-major variants. Confirm the scheduler module iterates over this registry when benchmarking.

sub_tasks.requirements: Each candidate variant exposes an identifier (name/enum) and a metadata record describing its tiling scheme (row-major vs column-major) and tile-size parameters so results can be logged per variant.

verification.spec: For each entry in the candidate-kernel registry, assert it exposes a 'name' (or enum) attribute and a 'metadata' record with fields describing tiling scheme ('row_major' or 'column_major') and tile-size parameters (BLOCK_M/N/K or equivalent). Assert names are unique.

sub_tasks.requirements: The row-major tiling variant is implemented to maximize reuse of input activation X across the fused W_Up/W_Gate GEMMs.

Code has been implemented in which the row-major variant iterates the outer loop over rows of the input/output tile such that an activation-row tile is loaded once from HBM and reused across the K-dimension GEMM accumulation for both W_Up and W_Gate.

verification.spec: Inspect source code of the row-major DeepFusionKernel variant (e.g., Triton/CUDA source file). Confirm that the outer loop iterates over rows of the input/output tile (M dimension), and that within an outer iteration an activation-row tile is loaded once (e.g., tl.load of X[m_block, :]) and reused across the K-dimension accumulation loop for both W_Up and W_Gate GEMMs. Grep for the loop structure and check that the activation load is hoisted outside the K-reduction and shared between the Up and Gate accumulations.

sub_tasks.requirements: The row-major variant stages activation tiles into shared memory (or registers) before issuing Tensor Core mma instructions, and does not re-load the same activation tile from HBM within a single output-tile computation.

verification.spec: Inspect the row-major kernel source. Confirm (a) activation tiles are staged into shared memory or registers (Triton implicit shared via tl.load into block-typed tensors used by tl.dot, or CUDA __shared__ / cp.async / ldmatrix into fragments feeding mma.sync/wgmma) before Tensor Core ops, and (b) within one output-tile computation the same activation tile is not re-loaded from HBM (verify by counting tl.load / cp.async / ldg calls on X inside the K-loop; expect a single load per K-block reused for both Up and Gate).

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test / correctness check verifies that the row-major variant produces outputs numerically matching (within FP16 tolerance) a reference SwiGLU (W_Up, W_Gate, SiLU, elementwise multiply) computation on random inputs.

verification.spec: Run a pytest that constructs random FP16 tensors X (shape e.g. [B*T, d_model]) and W_Up, W_Gate (shape [d_model, d_ff]) for representative shapes (e.g., d_model=1024, d_ff=3584, B*T in {1,4,16}). Invoke the row-major DeepFusionKernel to produce output Y_fused. Compute reference Y_ref = silu(X @ W_Gate) * (X @ W_Up) in FP16 (or via FP32 accumulation cast to FP16). Assert torch.allclose(Y_fused, Y_ref, atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2) or max abs diff below FP16 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: The column-major tiling variant is implemented to maximize reuse of weight tiles from W_Up and W_Gate, favoring small-batch / weight-dominated regimes.

Code has been implemented in which the column-major variant iterates the outer loop over output columns (weight-column tiles) so that a loaded W_Up/W_Gate tile is reused across multiple activation rows before being evicted.

sub_tasks.requirements: Method components (from critique splits and additions)

Code has been implemented such that DeepFusionKernel produces numerically equivalent SwiGLU MLP outputs compared to the reference (SGLang / PyTorch) implementation, verifying fusion correctness before measuring speedup

verification.spec: Construct a SwiGLU MLP block with d_model=8192, d_ff=28672 (Llama 3.1 70B shapes) in FP16 on GPU. Run both the DeepFusionKernel fused implementation and a reference two-kernel (SGLang-style: fused up/gate GEMM + SiLU*Mul + Down GEMM) implementation on the same random input. Assert torch.allclose(out_fused, out_reference, atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2)

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the fused Up and Gate GEMMs share the same X tile load and iterate over the K (d_model) dimension jointly within a single kernel, so each X tile is loaded from HBM exactly once and used to update both Up and Gate accumulators.

verification.spec: Statically inspect the fused kernel source (CUDA/Triton). Assert that (a) there is exactly one outer K-loop over d_model, (b) X is loaded into shared memory / registers once per K-tile iteration, and (c) both Up and Gate MMA/dot accumulators are updated inside that same K-loop body using the shared X tile. Fail if X is loaded twice or if Up and Gate have separate K-loops.
verification.paper_cite: Section 3 and Figure 1(c): 'single, deeply fused kernel that streams data through GEMMs and nonlinearities'

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that SiLU activation on the Up accumulator and elementwise multiplication with the Gate accumulator are performed in registers on the MMA accumulator values before any epilogue store to shared memory or HBM.

verification.spec: Inspect the fused kernel source. Assert that (a) SiLU (x * sigmoid(x)) is applied to the Up accumulator variable in the kernel's register-resident epilogue region, (b) the multiplication with the Gate accumulator occurs on register variables, and (c) neither the pre-SiLU Up tile nor the post-SiLU tile is written to shared memory or HBM before the multiply. Fail if a store-then-reload pattern is detected between the GEMM and the SiLU/Mul.
verification.paper_cite: Section 3 / Figure 1(c): SiLU and Mul are fused inside the single kernel

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that no intermediate (M, d_ff/TP) activation tensor is materialized in HBM between the fused Up/Gate/SiLU/Mul kernel and the subsequent W_Down GEMM, verified via HBM traffic measurement.

verification.spec: For a representative shape (M=16, d_model=8192, d_ff/TP≈7168 for Llama-3.1-70B TP=4), run the fused kernel followed by W_Down under Nsight Compute (or CUPTI dram__bytes counter). Compute HBM bytes read+written attributable to the fused kernel's OUTPUT and W_Down's LEFT INPUT. Assert this is <= (M * d_ff/TP * dtype_bytes) * 1.2 counting only the single hand-off write+read (i.e., roughly one materialization), and strictly less than 2x that (which would indicate a separate intermediate buffer plus reload). Compare against a two-kernel SGLang baseline which should show ~2x this traffic.
verification.paper_cite: Section 3: 'streams intermediate values through the computation, avoiding materialization of large temporaries and drastically cutting reads/writes to HBM'
